what_happened: Confirmed via direct re-execution of plan-file-scope-harvest.sh against the real archived #417 plan that the harvester's grammar already matches plan-format.md's documented 'one path per Files-to-modify line' contract exactly; the 4 missing paths were a plan-authoring deviation (comma-join and wrapped-continuation lines), not a harvester bug. Rejected widening the harvester's token scan because the same block contains non-path backtick tokens (a quoted markdown heading, a bare basename missing its directory) that would become garbage file_scope entries.

Discovered a live, present-day loophole while root-causing the #424 citation: archived task 424's file_scope still holds the literal entry '.claude/' (harvested from that plan's own Phase 4 Files-to-modify block, which named .claude/ directly instead of plan-format.md's reserved __WHOLE_TREE__ sentinel). Empirically re-tested today's (already-fixed, post-2a945dca3) is_contained() trailing-slash normalization against this entry: it now judges every .claude/** path as CONTAINED, the inverse of the Hard Constraint's intent. Neither plan-file-scope-harvest.sh nor validate-artifact.sh currently refuses a harvested .claude/** path. Recorded as a PART A recommendation (harvester refusal + validate-artifact.sh advisory check) in the research report rather than fixed here (research-only dispatch).

The research report's per-citation verdict table and its five numbered Decisions mapped one-to-one onto phase boundaries with no re-derivation: the only new plan-stage work was (1) re-measuring suite_selection_select per phase for Tier Justifications and (2) discovering a third leak path the report did not name (propose_file_scope_addition() can itself deposit a .claude/** path into proposed_file_scope, which implement-postflight then merges into state.json's file_scope) -- folded into Phase 3 as a deposit-site refusal.

test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh fails (25/304) when run via the Phase 2 Tier Justification suite set, but confirmed pre-existing and unrelated: no diff exists for that suite or its target scripts (orchestrator-postflight.sh, update-task-status.sh) since this task's own Phase 1 commit, and the failures (status-name mismatches like 'planning' vs 'researching', persisted_status drift) bear no relation to the Files-to-modify authoring-shape check this phase added. Not touched by this task's declared file_scope. Verification for Phase 2 relied on the directly relevant suites (test-validate-artifact.sh, test-plan-file-scope-harvest.sh), both green.

git-commit-phase.sh's deployed-tree strip (Phase 3) only closes the .claude/** loophole at its OWN Containment Self-Check (Site 2 of the documented three containment sites). git-commit-scoped.sh carries a separate, unpatched V10 containment guard (Site 3) that re-reads the unstripped file_scope directly from specs/state.json; neither git-commit-scoped.sh nor its test suite are members of this task's declared file_scope, so patching Site 3 was out of scope. Discovered via a test fixture (Case 26 in test-git-commit-phase.sh) with a file_scope of solely '.claude/': Site 2 correctly fails open (skips its own check entirely), but Site 3 independently still judges a files_touched path not otherwise carve-out-admitted as uncontained and drops it from the actual commit pathspec, via its OWN un-patched is_contained_v10(). The test was narrowed to assert only Site 2's own behavior (no drop warning, nothing proposed) rather than the full end-to-end commit outcome, to avoid masking this residual by weakening the assertion to match Site 3's unrelated behavior. A full architectural closure would need the SAME deployed-tree strip ported to git-commit-scoped.sh's V10 resolution block (around its containment_scope_arr assembly), which this task does not do.
